topics.title: 字母与发音
topics.description: 英语字母及汉语中没有的发音

guide.intro: 英语字母表由 26 个字母组成——与汉语拼音相比，包含 Q、W、X 等字母。重点不在书写而在发音：英语里有些声音在汉语中完全不存在。

rows: 无——不是 z，舌头在齿间
介于 a 与 e 之间的开口音

sections.text: 学习者最常见的错误：把「think」念成「tink」或「sink」。发「th」音时把舌尖轻轻放在上齿之间然后吹气。
W 与 V 的区别
汉语中没有「w」与「v」的对立。英语里这两个是不同的音，混淆会改变词义：「wine」（葡萄酒）和「vine」（藤蔓）是不同的词。发「W」时双唇像念「u」一样拢圆。

items: Q: queen, quick——几乎总是「qu」=「kw」音
W: window, week——双唇拢圆
X: box, six——「ks」音

topics.title: 问候语
topics.description: 你好、再见和你好吗

guide.intro: 英语问候因时段和场合正式程度而变化。汉语「你好」可以在任何场合使用，而英语需要掌握几种不同的说法。

sections.text: 「Good night」类似汉语的「晚安」——只用于睡前或夜里告别——不是晚上的问候语。晚上见面要说「Good evening」。
汉语里回答「你好吗？」只说「很好」就够了；英语中说「I'm fine, thanks. And you?」更礼貌——反问对方是惯例。

topics.title: 代词
topics.description: I、you、he、she、it 以及性别区分

guide.intro: 汉语里「他/她/它」发音相同，只在字形上有别。英语用三个完全不同的代词：he（男性）、she（女性）、it（无生命/动物）。这是学习者最易出错的语法点之一。

sections.text: 汉语「他/她」发音相同，所以学习者经常把女性说成「he」。指女性时要记得用「she」：「My sister... she is nice.」。最常见的错误是给女性用「he」。
汉语「我」可以小写。英语中只有一个字母的代词「I」必须永远大写——即使在句子中间。

exercises.explanation: 英语中「you」既表示单数「你」也表示复数「你们」；没有区别。

exercises.prompt: 下面这个句子有错：「i am happy.」错在哪里？

topics.title: Be 动词（am/is/are）
topics.description: 汉语中“是”在英语中的不同形式

guide.intro: 汉语「我是学生」用一个「是」字。英语必须用「I am a student.」——「to be」根据主语变化为 am、is、are 三种形式。

sections.text: 汉语里形容词句子常常没有动词：「他很开心。」英语必须有「to be」：「He is happy.」——遗漏「is/am/are」是最常见的错误。

guide.intro: 汉语没有「a/an/the」这样的冠词。「我读了一本书」中的「一本」有点像不定冠词。英语中可数单数名词前必须加「a/an」或「the」。

guide.intro: 汉语里说「下雨」或「冷」可以没有主语——动词和形容词单独成句。英语里的天气句子总是以「It is ...」或「It + 动词」开头。这里的「it」没有具体含义——只是语法上必须有主语。

sections.text: 汉语「冷。」可以单独成句；英语「Cold.」单独不成句，要说「It is cold.」。这里的「it」不代表「它」——是没有实际意义的语法主语。
汉语问「天气怎么样？」。英语用「How is the weather?」或「What's the weather like?」。
注意区别：「rains」与「is raining」不同。「It rains in winter」（冬天下雨——泛指）与「It is raining now」（现在正在下雨）含义不同。

exercises.explanation: hot = 热（温度）；sunny = 晴（太阳的状态）。

exercises.explanation: cool = 凉爽（既不太冷也不太热）。

topics.title: 地点
topics.description: 家、学校、商店等地点以及“在哪里？”的提问

guide.intro: 汉语用「在……」表示位置：「在家」、「在学校」、「在公园」。英语根据地点不同要用不同的介词：in、at、on。最常用的是「in」（里面）和「at」（在某一具体地点）。

sections.text: 汉语的「在」在英语里要分三个词：「in」（在……里面——较大的地方、城市）、「at」（在某一具体点——地址、地点名称）、「on」（在……上面——表面之上）。

topics.title: 一般过去时 (Past Simple)
topics.description: 用规则和不规则动词讲述过去

guide.intro: 汉语中表示过去常用「了」或时间词(昨天、上周等);英语则用一般过去时 (past simple) 来表达。动词分为两类:规则动词(加 -ed)和不规则动词(特殊形式)。所有人称形式都相同——不像汉语那样需要靠时间词,而是动词本身变化。

sections.text: 拼写规则:辅音字母 + y 结尾 → 变 y 为 i 再加 ed:study → studied。单音节 + 单辅音字母 → 双写辅音再加 ed:stop → stopped。以 e 结尾 → 只加 d:live → lived。
用了「didn't」或「did」后,动词要用原形:「I didn't went」错误,「I didn't go」正确。中文学习者容易习惯性地再加 -ed,这是常见错误。

topics.title: 现在进行时 (Present Continuous)
topics.description: 正在发生的动作

guide.intro: 汉语中说「正在……」或在动作后加「着/呢」来表示正在进行;英语用「am/is/are + 动词-ing」结构。例如:「我正在去」=「I am going」。要注意它和一般现在时(表习惯)的区别:一般现在时讲习惯,现在进行时讲此刻正在发生的事。

sections.text: 汉语中的「正在……」相当于英语的「-ing」结构。「我正在吃饭」=「I am eating」。「am/is/are」起到连接动作和主语的作用,务必不要省略。

guide.intro: 现在完成时是英语中最易让人困惑的时态,因为中文里没有完全对应的形式。有时翻成「已经……过」(「已经去过」),有时翻成现在时(「我住了三年了」),有时翻成过去时(「我从来没去过」)。核心理念:动作开始于过去,与现在仍有联系。

sections.text: have/has + fiilin 3. hali (V3, past participle). Olumsuz: haven't/hasn't + V3. Soru: Have/Has + özne + V3?

guide.intro: 情态动词承担了英语语气一半的功能。中文里表示「能/会」(能力/可能性)、「应该/必须」(义务) 的说法,在英语里对应好几个不同的情态动词。选错情态动词可能会完全改变句意。

sections.text: Modal + V1 (yalın fiil). Modaller -s almaz, -ed almaz, do/does ile soru kurmaz. Olumsuz: modal + not.

'May' biraz daha yüksek olasılık ve daha resmi. 'Might' düşük olasılık. İkisi de 'belki' ile çevrilebilir ama ton farklıdır.

guide.intro: 中文表示被动的「被/由」结构,在英语里对应「be + V3」句型。中文常用被动结构,英语则更挑剔。被动句用来淡化或隐藏动作的发出者。

sections.text: Aktiften pasife: aktifteki nesne pasifin öznesi olur; fiil 'be + V3' biçimine girer; eylemi yapan 'by + agent' ile gösterilir (zorunlu değil).

items: 动作发出者未知:「My phone was stolen.」

描述过程时:「The coffee is roasted, ground, and served.」

sections.text: Türk öğrenenlerin sık hatası: Türkçedeki 'kahve içilir' tarzı genel ifadeleri İngilizcede de pasifle vermek. İngilizce konuşma dilinde aktif daha doğaldır: 'People drink coffee here' ya da 'We drink coffee here'.
Pasifte fiilin 3. halini (V3) doğru bilmek şart. 'Was wrote' YANLIŞ; doğrusu 'was written'. 'Was eat' YANLIŞ; doğrusu 'was eaten'.

topics.title: 短语动词 (Phrasal Verbs)
topics.description: look up、give up、run into 及其他

guide.intro: 短语动词是英语最大的难点之一,因为中文里几乎没有这种结构。像「Look up」(不是「看」,而是「查询」)、「give up」(不是「给」,而是「放弃」),整体含义和单个动词不同。口语中用短语动词更自然;正式书面语更倾向拉丁语源的对应词(research、surrender)。

rows: 锻炼 / 解决 / 进展顺利

sections.text: Bazı phrasal verb'ler nesneyle ARALARINA girebilir (ayrılabilir / separable). Bazıları AYRILMAZ (inseparable). Zamir nesne (it, him, them) ayrılabilirlerde ZORUNLU olarak araya girer.

rows.source: 可分离:I looked up the word. / I looked the word up.
代词形式:I looked it up.(I looked up it. 是错的)
不可分离:I ran into John.(I ran John into. 是错的)
不可分离:She gets along with her sister.

sections.text: İpucu: Phrasal verb'leri tek tek ezberleyin, ipuçlarına güvenmeyin. 'Look up' (araştır) ile 'look down on' (küçük görmek) arasında mantıksal bağ yok — sözlükten teyit edin.

topics.title: B1 综合复习
topics.description: 整合所有 B1 主题的综合复习

guide.intro: 整合 B1 六大主题的复习单元:现在完成时、情态动词、条件句、被动语态、短语动词和假朋友词汇。在每一课中你都会做到至少一道来自每个主题的练习。

items: 现在完成时:have/has + V3 — 从过去延伸到现在的动作。
情态动词:must (义务)、should (建议)、can/could (能力/许可)、may/might (可能)。
条件句:zero (普遍真理)、first (可能的将来)、second (假想的现在)。
被动:be + V3 — 动作者不重要或未知。
短语动词:动词 + 介词 → 整体含义(要记忆)。
假朋友词汇:「actual」= 实际的;「library」= 图书馆;「chef」= 厨师。

sections.text: Bu tekrar bölümünde 3 ders var, her biri farklı konuları karıştırır. Hatalarını not et — hangi konuda hâlâ takıldığını gösterir.

levels.name: B2 — 中高级
levels.description: 讨论抽象话题、表达观点、阅读新闻并在工作场合使用英语。重点关注复杂时态、条件句和语域差异。

topics.title: 表达和捍卫观点
topics.description: 如何阐述观点、如何缓和语气、如何反对

guide.intro: 在 B2 阶段,光说 「I think」 是不够的。英语母语者用各种缓和语气(hedging)的工具来表达观点。中文里的「我觉得」、「在我看来」、「我猜」 这些细微的差别在英语中都有对应说法 —— 但并非一一对应。

sections.text: 在英语中表达观点时,调整语气的强度很重要。「I think」 是中性的;「I believe」 略强一些;「I'd argue」 带有辩论的色彩;「It seems to me」 较为间接。
英语母语者常常会缓和自己的观点。「sort of」、「kind of」、「I guess」 这类填充词在中文中很难找到完全对等的说法。它们并不显得犹豫,而是体现礼貌。

rows.source: I sort of agree, but I have one concern.
rows.translation: [[MISSING:Bir nevi katılıyorum ama bir kaygım var.]]

rows.source: It's kind of complicated, to be honest.
I'd say it's more nuanced than that.

sections.text: 在英语中直接说 「You are wrong」 太过生硬。更可取的说法包括 「I see your point, but…」、「I'm not sure I agree」 或 「I have to disagree」。
中文里「我不同意」 是一句很直接的话;但在英语商务场合,不加缓和地直接说出来会显得粗鲁。「I'd have to respectfully disagree」 是更稳妥的说法。

rows.source: I see where you're coming from, but I'd push back on that.
rows.translation: [[MISSING:Ne demek istediğini anlıyorum ama buna itiraz ederim.]]

rows.source: With all due respect, I don't quite agree.
rows.translation: [[MISSING:Saygısızlık etmek istemem ama tam olarak katılmıyorum.]]

rows.source: That's a fair point, although I'd add that…
rows.translation: [[MISSING:Haklı bir nokta, yine de şunu eklerdim ki…]]

exercises.prompt: 「It seems to me that…」 在中文里相当于什么意思?
exercises.explanation: 「It seems to me」 用委婉的方式表达个人印象。

exercises.prompt: 「我觉得这个想法合理」 最自然的英文翻译是哪个?
options: By me, this idea makes logic.
I think this idea makes sense.
From me, this idea is logic.
In my opinion this idea is logical for me.
exercises.answer: I think this idea makes sense.
exercises.explanation: 「Make sense」 = 「合理、说得通」。「Make logic」 是错误搭配。

exercises.prompt: 「___ argue that remote work boosts productivity.」(中文:「我会说远程工作提升了效率。」)
exercises.explanation: 「I'd argue」 表达带有辩论色彩的观点。

exercises.prompt: 把英文句型与中文释义配对
造句:「依我看,这个计划不现实。」
exercises.answer: As far as I'm concerned this plan is not realistic
exercises.explanation: 「As far as I'm concerned」 接近中文里「依我看」 的句型。

exercises.spokenText: I'd argue that the policy needs revision.
options: I'd argue that the policy needs revision.
I argue the policy needs vision.
I'd agree that the policy needs revision.
I argued the police need revision.
exercises.answer: I'd argue that the policy needs revision.
exercises.explanation: 「I'd argue」 = 「I would argue」;用于表达带辩论色彩的观点。

exercises.prompt: 「___ my mind, the proposal lacks substance.」(中文:「依我看,这个提议不够有深度。」)
哪一句表达了最强烈的观点?
options: I sort of think it's fine.
I'm firmly convinced this is the right path.
It seems to me this might work.
exercises.answer: I'm firmly convinced this is the right path.
exercises.explanation: 「Firmly convinced」 = 「坚定地相信」。其他选项都带有缓和。

exercises.prompt: 造句:「从我的角度看,这个解决方案不够。」
exercises.answer: From my perspective this solution is inadequate

exercises.prompt: 「Honestly, I ___ convinced.」 填空(中文:「老实说,我并未完全被说服。」)
exercises.explanation: 「Not entirely convinced」 是一种委婉的反对句型。

lessons.title: 缓和语气(hedging)

options: 缓和句子,降低肯定程度

With all the respect, I had to disagree.
Without due respect, I have to agree.

lessons.title: 为观点提供论据
lessons.description: 用 「because」、「given that」、「considering」 支持你的观点

exercises.prompt: 在 「Given that we have limited time, I'd suggest postponing the launch.」 中,「given that」 是什么意思?
「我是根据数据做出这个决定的」 最自然的英文是?
options: I made this decision in lights of the data.
I made this decision in the light of the data.
I made this decision under data lights.
I made this decision in data light.
exercises.answer: I made this decision in the light of the data.

exercises.prompt: 哪一句对观点提出了最有力的论证?
options: I think it's fine because of reasons.
I'd argue it's the right call given the recent data and our team's bandwidth.
exercises.answer: I'd argue it's the right call given the recent data and our team's bandwidth.

exercises.prompt: 「___ that the deadline has been moved, we should reprioritize.」(中文:「鉴于截止日期被推后,我们应当重新调整优先级。」)
exercises.explanation: 「Now that」 / 「Given that」 / 「Seeing that」 起同样作用。

exercises.prompt: 「I take this view ___ several reasons.」 填空。
「My position is grounded ___ recent research.」(中文:「……立足于最新的研究。」)

Considered budget cuts, I think we scaled back.
exercises.answer: Considering the budget cuts, I think we should scale back.

exercises.prompt: 造句:「鉴于当前的情况,这一举动显得有风险。」

topics.title: 理解新闻
topics.description: 破解新闻标题,跟读新闻文本

guide.intro: 英语新闻语言自成一体:标题简短、被动结构、引述动词,以及高频固定搭配。对中文学习者来说,陷阱在于中文新闻措辞(尤其是与拉丁词根相关的)并不一定一一对应到英语。例如「实际的」在英语中并不一定是 「actual」,而 「actual」 实际上意味着「真正的、实际存在的」 —— 这是经典的「假朋友」(false friend)。

sections.text: 英语新闻标题通常使用现在时(即使是过去发生的事件),省略 「a/the」 冠词,并用不定式表示将来。

rows: The PM has resigned amid a scandal
A tech firm is going to acquire its rival
科技公司将收购竞争对手
Three people are dead in a factory explosion
工厂爆炸造成 3 人死亡

sections.text: 新闻报道中不会每句都用 「said」,而是用 「claimed」、「stated」、「announced」、「reported」、「denied」 等带有不同语气的动词。每一个的语气都不一样。
中文里的「声称」 并不总是 「claimed」。正式声明用 「stated」 或 「announced」 更恰当。「claimed」 在英语中通常带有怀疑意味。
新闻语言中,若主语不明或不重要,会倾向使用被动结构:「Three people were arrested」、「A new policy is being introduced」。

rows.source: The bill is expected to pass next week.
rows.translation: 据报道该法案预计将于下周通过。

rows.source: The minister was reported to have stepped down.

lessons.title: 破解新闻标题

exercises.prompt: 哪一项是标准的新闻标题缩短方式?

guide.intro: 要在 B2 水平讨论环境话题,搭配(collocations)非常关键。要说 「take action」,而不说 「do action」;说 「reduce emissions」,「lower emissions」 也行,但 「shrink emissions」 听起来就很别扭。

sections.text: 讨论环境时常常涉及可能性和必要性。「must」、「should」、「ought to」、「might」、「could」 表达不同程度。「We must cut emissions」 是强烈必要;「We could explore alternatives」 是温和建议。

rows.source: Governments must take immediate action on climate change.

rows.source: We could reduce our carbon footprint by switching to renewables.
rows.translation: 我们可以通过转向可再生能源来减少碳足迹。

rows.source: Without intervention, biodiversity loss is bound to accelerate.
rows.translation: 若不采取干预,生物多样性丧失必将加速。

sections.text: 「bound to」 = 「必定会/必定已发生」,是强势的推测。相当于中文的「不可避免」 的力度。

guide.intro: 情绪是普世的,但在不同语言中的表达方式并不一样。英语中表达情绪常用「形容词 + feel」 结构:「I feel overwhelmed」、「She felt let down」。中文里这些情绪常用动词或动宾结构表达:「我感到压力山大」、「我很失望」。

topics.title: 条件句与混合结构
topics.description: 学习第二、第三和混合条件句

guide.intro: B2 阶段的条件句不只是 if 从句的规则;它是表达推测、遗憾和假设性思考的工具。中文里的「如果……就……」 结构与英语第三类条件句(third conditional)有相似之处,但并不完全相同。

sections.text: 如果过去的决定影响到当下的情况,就使用混合条件句:「If I had studied harder, I would have a better job now」 = 「如果我当时更努力学习,现在就会有一份更好的工作」。

rows.source: If I were you, I'd take the offer.
rows.translation: 如果我是你,我会接受这个提议。

rows.source: If she had left earlier, she'd be home by now.
rows.translation: 如果她早点出发,现在就到家了。

rows.source: Had I known, I would have called.
rows.translation: 我要是知道,就会打电话了。

sections.text: 正式写作中,像 「Had I known」 这种没有 if 的倒装结构非常考究。在 C1 阶段会更常见;在 B2 阶段能识别即可。

guide.intro: 英语中,在口语和正式书面语中表达同一意思时用词不同。「get」 在日常会话中无所不能,但正式书面语中更倾向于 「receive」、「obtain」、「become」 等选项。

sections.text: 对不认识的人:「Dear Mr/Ms [姓]」。熟悉但仍属职业关系:「Hi [名]」。内部同事之间:「Hey [名]」 可以接受。结尾:「Sincerely」(最正式)、「Best regards」(标准)、「Best」/「Cheers」(亲切)。

sections.text: 中文里的「此致敬礼」 并不总是对应 「Sincerely」。正式申请用 「Yours sincerely」(英)、「Sincerely」(美)。给同事用 「Best regards」 就够了。

topics.title: 被动语态与复杂时态
topics.description: 过去完成时、将来完成时、情态被动

guide.intro: 在 B2 阶段,时态轴变得更精细。你将学习被动语态在各种时态中的形式,以及如何与情态动词结合。

sections.text: 过去完成时 — 更早的过去
过去完成时(had + V3)表示两个过去事件中较早发生的那个:「When I arrived, they had already left」 = 「我到达时,他们已经离开了」。相当于中文里的「曾经……了」 结构。

rows.source: By the time we got there, the meeting had ended.
rows.translation: 我们到那里时,会议已经结束了。

rows.source: She had never seen such a sight before.
rows.translation: 她之前从未见过这样的景象。

rows.source: The report had been reviewed by the board.
rows.translation: 报告已经被董事会审阅过了。

sections.text: 将来完成时(will have + V3)表示在未来某个时点已经完成的事情。「By 2030, AI will have transformed many industries」 = 「到 2030 年,人工智能将已经改造了许多行业」。

topics.title: 教育与学术生活
topics.description: 学校体系、学习习惯、考试词汇,以及英式英语与美式英语教育术语的差异

guide.intro: B2 阶段谈论教育不只是说一句 「I go to school」。各国教育体系不同,英式英语(BrE)和美式英语(AmE)的术语也有差异,描述学习习惯的动词(如 「cram」、「revise」、「retain」)也无法直接翻译成中文。

sections.text: 大多数国家的教育分为三个阶段:初等(primary)、中等(secondary)和高等(tertiary)。「Compulsory education」 = 「义务教育」。
中文里的「学习」 在英语中有多种细分:「study」=泛指学习;「revise」(英式)=复习;「cram」=临时突击;「memorize」=背诵;「grasp」=理解;「retain」=记住知识。

rows.source: I crammed all night for the exam.
rows.translation: 我整晚临时抱佛脚准备考试。

rows.source: You shouldn't just memorize — try to grasp the underlying ideas.
rows.translation: 不要只是死记硬背 —— 要努力理解核心概念。

rows.source: I find it hard to retain information when I'm tired.
rows.translation: 我累的时候很难记住知识。

rows.source: I need to brush up on my French before the trip.
rows.translation: 出行前我得复习一下我的法语。

sections.text: 英式英语 「sit an exam」 = 美式英语 「take an exam」。成绩相关习语:「pass with flying colours」(以优异成绩通过)、「scrape through」(勉强通过)、「fail miserably」(惨败)、「ace an exam」(考得极好)。
英式英语里的 「public school」 实际上是收费的、高端的私立学校 —— 并不是「公立学校」。这是一个容易混淆的术语。英式英语中「公立学校」 用 「state school」。

rows.translation: 我考砸了之后不得不补考。

topics.title: 辩论与反对
topics.description: 在职业/社交场合礼貌反对、让步、寻找共识的句型

guide.intro: B2 阶段的辩论已远不止 「I agree / I disagree」 那么简单。在职业场合直接反对会显得粗鲁;然而一味同意又显得被动。解决之道是:先认可,再委婉提出异议。这与中文里「你说得有道理,但……」 之类的句型相似。

sections.text: 英语中有许多现成的反对句型。「I beg to differ」 正式且礼貌;「with all due respect」 略带防御性;「I'm not so sure」 很委婉;「on the contrary」 直截了当但不带个人色彩。

rows: I'm not so sure about that

sections.text: 让步 + 反驳(concede + push back)
高效的辩论者会先部分认可对方,再坚持自己的主张。「Granted, …」、「Fair point, but …」、「I take your point, however …」 都属于此类。

rows.source: Granted, the costs are high, but the long-term benefits outweigh them.
rows.translation: 承认成本很高,但长期收益远超于此。

rows.source: Fair point, but I still think the timing is off.
rows.translation: 你说得有道理,但我仍然觉得时机不对。

rows.source: I take your point; that said, the data tells a different story.
rows.translation: 我明白你的意思;不过数据讲了一个不同的故事。

sections.text: 在会议中礼貌插话可以说 「If I may, …」/「May I jump in?」/「Sorry to interrupt, but …」。请求进一步解释时,可以说 「Could you elaborate?」/「Could you clarify what you mean?」。
中文里「我当然不同意」 这种程度的反对,如果直接译为 「Of course I disagree」 会显得过于生硬。改用 「I'm afraid I have to disagree」 或 「I'd respectfully push back on that」 —— 同样清晰,但语气好得多。
最后,用 「find common ground」(寻找共识)、「meet in the middle」(各让一步)、「reach a compromise」(达成妥协)、「agree to disagree」(求同存异)等表达,可以成熟地结束辩论。

rows.source: Why don't we meet in the middle on this?
rows.translation: 我们在这件事上各让一步好吗?

rows.source: All things considered, I think we've found a workable compromise.
rows.translation: 综合考虑,我认为我们已经达成了一个可行的妥协。
我们就当我们意见不同好了。

topics.title: 商务英语
topics.description: 会议、谈判与正式书面沟通

guide.intro: 商务英语生存于远高于日常用语的语域中。报告中常用 「in light of」、「given the fact that」、「on account of」 来替代日常的 「because」。C1 阶段要教的不仅是词汇,更是如何始终保持语域的一致性。

sections.text: 正式语域中的因果连接词
「Because」 属于日常口语。在正式写作中,人们更倾向使用 「in view of」、「given that」、「in light of」、「owing to」。「Therefore」、「hence」、「consequently」 看似同义,但 「hence」 略显文言,「consequently」 则带有更浓的学术色彩。
在商务谈判中,说「不」的方式有几十种。「I'm afraid that won't be possible」、「We may have difficulty meeting that figure」、「Let me get back to you on that」 都是委婉的拒绝。中文里那种间接拒绝的反射(例如「现在很难」)在英语谈判中起到相同的作用。

rows.source: I'm afraid that won't be feasible at this stage.

rows.source: We may have difficulty meeting that figure.
rows.translation: 我们可能难以达到这个数字。

rows.source: Let me get back to you on that.
rows.translation: 关于这一点,我回头再答复您。

rows.source: I'd like to push back on that timeline.
rows.translation: 我想对这一时间表提出异议。

sections.text: 在英语商务环境中,关键不仅在于选词,更在于你的措辞有多委婉。从中文切换到英语的专业人士常犯的错误是:直接说 「It is not possible」 就戛然而止。更自然的版本是:「I'm afraid that may not be feasible right now — perhaps we could explore an alternative?」

topics.title: 学术英语
topics.description: 构建论证、引用来源、答辩论文

guide.intro: 学术英语将论断与证据绑定,使用模糊语,并倾向名词化表达。中文学术风格往往容许长句;而英语学术风格则偏好简洁清晰的句子、明确的论点和带有模糊语的阐释。

sections.text: 学者们不会直接说 「X is true」,而会写 「The data suggest that X may be the case」。这是一种礼貌的克制:数据可能改变,也存在其他解读。
学术英语偏爱把动词改写为名词:不说 「They decided to invest」,而说 「The decision to invest…」 或 「Their investment decision…」。这能使句子更紧凑,也使语气更客观。

rows.source: The findings suggest that climate policy may have unintended effects.
rows.translation: 研究结果表明,气候政策可能存在未曾预料的副作用。

rows.source: A growing body of evidence indicates that…
This study seeks to address that gap.
rows.translation: 本研究旨在填补这一空白。

sections.text: 学术写作中很少出现 「I think」,取而代之的是 「It is argued that」、「this paper contends that」。这相当于中文学术风格中用「认为」「学界普遍认为」来替代「我觉得」的偏好。

lessons.title: 模糊语与主张力度

请组合出这个句子:「本研究旨在填补这一空白。」

exercises.prompt: 「It is argued that…」 是什么意思?

options: The findings appear to support our hypothesis.
The findings appears to support our hypothesis.
The findings appear to supports our hypothesis.
The finding appear to support our hypotheses.

exercises.prompt: 请组合出这个句子:「数据表明,该假设无法被拒绝。」

请组合出这个句子:「本研究提出了一个新的理论框架。」

exercises.prompt: 「In contrast to prior literature, we find…」 用中文该怎么说?

options: Drawing on prior research, we extend the framework.

exercises.answer: Drawing on prior research, we extend the framework.

exercises.prompt: 「The findings have important ___ for policy.」(中文:「这些发现对政策具有重要的意义。」)

exercises.prompt: 请组合出这个句子:「研究结果表明,现有理论存在不足。」

exercises.answer: The effect is similar across genders

options: Sağlam, farklı kontroller altında bozulmayan etki
exercises.answer: Sağlam, farklı kontroller altında bozulmayan etki

exercises.spokenText: The correlation is statistically significant at the one percent level.
options: The correlation is statistically significant at the one percent level.
The correlation is statically significant at the one percent level.
The correlation are statistically significant at the one percent level.
The correlations is statistically significant at the one percent levels.
exercises.answer: The correlation is statistically significant at the one percent level.

exercises.prompt: 「The sample is ___ relatively small.」(中文:「然而,样本量相对较小。」)

lessons.title: 学术综合 — 复习
lessons.description: 论文、模糊语与数据阐释

exercises.prompt: 「Notwithstanding these caveats, the results suggest…」 用中文怎么说?
options: Bu çekincelere rağmen sonuçlar… imâ etmektedir.
exercises.answer: Bu çekincelere rağmen sonuçlar… imâ etmektedir.

exercises.prompt: 「The results are robust ___ a number of specifications.」(中文:「在多种模型设定下,结果均稳健。」)
请组合出这个句子:「我们在本文中提出了一种新的机制。」

exercises.prompt: 学术连接词 — 中文释义

exercises.spokenText: The literature suggests that this effect is well-established.
options: The literature suggests that this effect is well-established.
The literature suggest that this effect is well established.
The literature suggests that this effects is well-established.
The literatures suggest that this effect is well-established.
exercises.answer: The literature suggests that this effect is well-established.

exercises.prompt: 下列哪一句包含主观个人主张?(在学术写作中通常需要回避)
options: I think we should reject the hypothesis.
The data appear to reject the hypothesis.
The hypothesis is rejected at the 1% level.
It is argued that the hypothesis can be rejected.
exercises.answer: I think we should reject the hypothesis.

exercises.prompt: 「Conversely, ___ found no such effect.」(中文:「相反,我们并未发现此类效应。」)
请组合出这个句子:「这些发现以三种方式为相关文献做出贡献。」
exercises.answer: The findings contribute to the literature in three ways

exercises.prompt: 「The effect is statistically ___」(中文:「该效应在统计学上是显著的。」)

lessons.title: 文献综述模式

exercises.prompt: 在文献综述中,「X 研究者主张……」 最恰当的英文表达是什么?
exercises.explanation: 在学术引用中,通常会标注年份并使用 「argues / contends / posits」。

exercises.prompt: 「Smith (2021) ___ a similar conclusion in a different setting.」(中文:「Smith 在另一情境下得出类似结论。」)

exercises.prompt: 「A growing body of research suggests that…」 这一句式的功能是什么?

exercises.spokenText: While prior work has focused on outcomes, the underlying processes remain underexplored.
options: While prior work has focused on outcomes, the underlying processes remain underexplored.
While prior works have focused on outcomes, the underlying process remain underexplored.
While prior work has focused on outcomes, the underlying processes remains underexplored.
While prior work had focused on outcome, the underlying processes remain underexplored.
exercises.answer: While prior work has focused on outcomes, the underlying processes remain underexplored.

exercises.prompt: 「This study seeks to ___ that gap in the literature.」(中文:「本研究旨在填补文献中的这一空白。」)
下列哪一句是用来表明「理论框架」的?
options: We use Maslow's hierarchy as our theoretical lens.
We have a lot of stuff in mind.
We thought of stuff and went with it.
Maslow is famous, so we used it.
exercises.answer: We use Maslow's hierarchy as our theoretical lens.
exercises.explanation: 「Theoretical lens / framework」 是学术写作的固定表达。

exercises.prompt: 请组合出这个句子:「研究结果在一定程度上反驳了先前的结论。」

exercises.prompt: 「Recent scholarship has called this assumption into ___」(中文:「近期学界对这一假设提出了质疑。」)
exercises.explanation: 「call sth into question」 = 使……受到质疑。

exercises.prompt: 下列哪一句是反驳某研究者论点的最学术化表达?

Smith doesn't know what he's talking about.
exercises.answer: However, Smith's account underestimates the role of context.

exercises.prompt: 请组合出这个句子:「围绕该议题尚未形成共识。」

lessons.title: 摘要写作
lessons.description: 高度浓缩的信息:目的、方法、发现、结论

exercises.prompt: 一篇摘要(abstract)通常按怎样的顺序写就?

Abstract 部分 — 典型动词/表达
请组合出这个句子:「本研究采用了混合方法的研究路径。」

exercises.answer: We sort of looked into how things turned out.
exercises.explanation: 「Sort of」 与 「turned out」 不符合摘要的语域要求。

exercises.spokenText: The findings have wider implications for policy and practice.
options: The findings have wider implications for policy and practice.
The finding have wider implication for policy and practice.
The findings has wider implications for policy and practice.
The findings have wider implication for policies and practice.
exercises.answer: The findings have wider implications for policy and practice.

exercises.prompt: 「Drawing ___ a sample of 240 firms, the analysis reveals…」(中文:「基于由 240 家公司组成的样本,分析揭示……」)

exercises.prompt: 「These findings ___ light on a long-standing debate.」(中文:「这些发现为一场长期存在的争论带来了启示。」)

lessons.title: 对话:论文答辩中的方法论质询

exercises.prompt: 论文答辩 — 提问与回答环节

turns.speaker: chair
turns.text: We'll open the floor. Professor Demir, your first line of questioning, please.

turns.speaker: exam
turns.text: Your sample is overwhelmingly drawn from urban respondents. How do you defend the generalisability of your claims?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 用学术模糊语承认局限,然后进行辩护
options: Yeah, that's a fair point, my sample is kind of weak there honestly.
I would readily concede the boundary, yet the patterns I identify hold across the urban strata I sampled, which I take pains to delimit in Chapter 4.
Generalisability isn't really my problem — the reader can decide.
turns.answer: I would readily concede the boundary, yet the patterns I identify hold across the urban strata I sampled, which I take pains to delimit in Chapter 4.

turns.speaker: exam
turns.text: Granted. But your coding scheme appears to collapse two analytically distinct constructs into one variable. Was that deliberate?

turns.speaker: you

turns.speaker: chair
turns.text: Thank you. We'll move to the second examiner after a brief pause.

guide.intro: 在社会议题的讨论中,词汇选择决定了政治语气。中文里的「国家」一词,在英语中可能对应 「state」、「government」 或 「public sector」,需视语境而定。C1 水平要求准确把握这些细微差别。

sections.text: 讨论社会议题时,既要立场鲜明,又要立场平衡:「There is a strong case for X, but…」、「On balance,…」、「It is widely acknowledged that…」。

rows.source: There is a strong case for reform.
rows.translation: 推行改革的理由非常充分。

rows.source: On balance, the policy has done more good than harm.
rows.translation: 总体而言,该政策利大于弊。

rows.source: It is widely acknowledged that the system is in need of overhaul.
rows.translation: 体系需要彻底改造这一点已被普遍接受。

sections.text: 英文 「liberal」 的含义因国而异:在美国偏左中,在英国偏中间偏中,在澳大利亚则是中右政党的名称。同一词汇带有截然不同的政治联想。

guide.intro: 习语是任何语言的心脏。C1 水平要求熟记 「cut to the chase」、「on the back burner」 这类习语。将中文习语直译过去往往是危险的:「小题大做」对应英文的 「make a mountain out of a molehill」 或 「blow it out of proportion」,而不是字面直译。

sections.text: 商务场景中流行的习语

rows: 关键问题 / 最终结论
off the top of my head

sections.text: 从中文到英语切换时,直接翻译习语是危险的做法。在断言「英语里有对应说法」之前,先查证一下。

rows.source: We need to bite the bullet.
rows.translation: 我们必须硬着头皮接受现实。

sections.text: 警惕「直译」习语的陷阱:中文「念叨个没完」在英语里并不是 「iron the head」,而是 「talk someone's ear off」 或 「drone on」。不要直译,要去寻找等效表达。

exercises.answer: Let's pick the low-hanging fruit first then tackle the hard problems

lessons.title: 假朋友(第二轮)与语域陷阱

exercises.prompt: 容易混淆的词对 — 正确用法

pairs.right: 能体谅的(不是「招人喜欢的」)

exercises.prompt: 「I am actually going to the meeting」 是什么意思?
exercises.explanation: 「actually」 = 其实/事实上;把它当作「现在」来用是错误的。

exercises.prompt: 「She is a very ___ person; she rarely overreacts.」(中文:「她是个非常明智的人,很少反应过度。」)
请组合出这个句子:「其实我们多年前就该解决这件事了。」
exercises.answer: Actually we should have solved this years ago

exercises.spokenText: I am sympathetic to your concern, but the policy stands.
options: I am sympathetic to your concern, but the policy stands.
I am sympathic to your concern, but the policy stand.
I am sympathetic to your concerns, but the policy stand.
I'm sympathetic to your concern, but the policies stands.
exercises.answer: I am sympathetic to your concern, but the policy stands.

exercises.prompt: 「The proposal is ___(意为可被辩护的),if not optimal.」(中文:「这一提议即便不是最优方案,也是可以被辩护的。」)
下列哪种描述准确?「I would like to invite you to please reply at your earliest convenience.」

exercises.answer: Aşırı resmi/kalabalık; 'I would appreciate a reply at your earliest convenience' daha akıcıdır

exercises.prompt: 请组合出这个句子:「我们应当寻找用更少词语表达同样意思的方式。」
exercises.answer: We should look for a way to say the same thing in fewer words

在商务语境中,「I'm comfortable with that」 最准确的含义是什么?
请组合出这个句子:「最后,我想就定价方面再提一点异议。」
exercises.answer: Finally I would like to push back on the pricing at one point

lessons.title: 对话:商务社交场合中的习语化交流
lessons.description: 与行业高管进行习语密集的寒暄

turns.speaker: exec
turns.text: Quite the turnout this year. Half the panels were preaching to the choir, if I'm honest.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 习语用得对吗?请选出正确的回答
options: Couldn't agree more — and the keynote felt like it was hedging its bets right up to the closing line.
Yeah the keynote was hedging the bet so big.
Couldn't more agree — the keynote was on fire of pants.
turns.answer: Couldn't agree more — and the keynote felt like it was hedging its bets right up to the closing line.

turns.speaker: vc
turns.text: Speaking of fence-sitters, what's your read on the regulation? Are people actually going to move, or is this all hot air?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 习语 — 在空白处填入正确的动词
turns.after: their cards close to their chest, but the early movers I've spoken to are quietly reallocating budget.

turns.speaker: exec
turns.text: Reallocation is one thing — execution is another beast entirely. Half of these initiatives die on the vine.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 选出符合 C1 水准的、紧扣习语语境的回答
options: Tell me about it — by the time procurement signs off, the window of opportunity has well and truly closed.
Tell me of it — when procurement signs, the window of chance is closing.
Tell me about it — by the time procurement signs off, the window of opportunity has totally yeeted itself.
turns.answer: Tell me about it — by the time procurement signs off, the window of opportunity has well and truly closed.

turns.speaker: vc
turns.text: So where are you placing your bets? Or is it too early in the evening for that conversation?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 习语 — 在空白处填入正确的动词
turns.before: Let's just say I'm keeping my powder
turns.after: until the next funding cycle clarifies the field.

turns.speaker: exec
turns.text: Wise. The last cohort of pre-emptive bets aged badly. A lot of egos got bruised.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 请选出语域合适的习语
options: True — though one or two of them turned out to be horses for courses; the timing just wasn't on their side.
True — those guys ate dirt big time, classic L.
True — they totally face-planted, you love to see it.
turns.answer: True — though one or two of them turned out to be horses for courses; the timing just wasn't on their side.

turns.speaker: vc
turns.text: Anyway, I should make the rounds before the bar runs dry. Let's pick this up over coffee next week.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Sounds good — I'll drop you a line in the morning to lock in a time.

topics.title: 高级语法:倒装与分裂句
topics.description: 用于强调的结构性工具

guide.intro: 在 C1 阶段,用不同的结构传达相同信息是制造重音的关键手段。倒装(inversion)、分裂句(cleft sentences)和前置(fronting)都是 C1 的标志性手法。

sections.text: 当否定或限制性副词位于句首时,主语与助动词需要调换位置:「Rarely have I seen such talent」、「Not only did he refuse, he also walked out」。
It-分裂句(It is X who/that…)与 What-分裂句(What I need is…)用于突出特定成分:「It was John who broke the vase」(打碎花瓶的是 John),「What I want is silence」(我想要的是安静)。

rows.source: It was Sarah who first noticed the error.
rows.translation: 最先注意到这一错误的人是 Sarah。

rows.source: What surprises me most is his silence.
rows.translation: 最让我惊讶的是他的沉默。

rows.source: Rarely have we encountered such resistance.
rows.translation: 我们很少遇到这样的抗拒。

rows.source: Not only is the policy ineffective, it is also costly.
rows.translation: 该政策不仅无效,而且代价高昂。

sections.text: 倒装多用于正式写作和演说;在日常对话中显得做作。你会在学术文章和新闻文本里经常见到。

exercises.prompt: 「我这辈子很少见过这样的才华」用正式的倒装句怎么表达?
options: I have rarely seen such talent in my life.
Rarely have I seen such talent in my life.
Rarely I have seen such talent in my life.
Rarely seen I such talent in my life.
exercises.answer: Rarely have I seen such talent in my life.

exercises.prompt: 「Never before ___ I felt such pressure.」(中文:「我此前从未感受过这样的压力。」)
请组合出这个句子:「他不仅拒绝,还离开了房间。」
exercises.answer: Not only did he refuse but he also walked out

exercises.prompt: 下列哪一句是正确的倒装句?
options: Hardly I had arrived when the storm broke.
Hardly had I arrived when the storm broke.
Hardly had I arrive when the storm broke.
Hardly I arrived when the storm broke.
exercises.answer: Hardly had I arrived when the storm broke.

exercises.spokenText: Under no circumstances should you reveal the source.
options: Under no circumstances should you reveal the source.
Under no circumstance should you reveal the source.
Under no circumstances should you revealed the source.
Under no circumstances you should reveal the source.
exercises.answer: Under no circumstances should you reveal the source.

exercises.prompt: 「No sooner ___ I sat down than the phone rang.」(中文:「我刚坐下电话就响了。」)
请组合出这个句子:「在任何情况下都不应让门保持敞开。」
exercises.answer: Under no circumstances should the door be left open

exercises.prompt: 「Little ___ they realise the danger.」(中文:「他们对那危险几乎毫无察觉。」)
exercises.explanation: 「Little did they realise」 是惯用的倒装表达。

exercises.prompt: 「最先注意到错误的是 Sarah」 用英语怎么说?
options: It was Sarah who first noticed the error.
exercises.answer: It was Sarah who first noticed the error.

exercises.prompt: 「___ surprises me most is his silence.」(中文:「最让我惊讶的是他的沉默。」)
请组合出这个句子:「我真正需要的是时间。」
exercises.answer: What I really need is time

exercises.prompt: 分裂句结构 — 强调重心
「It was in 2008 that the crisis hit」 用中文怎么翻译?

exercises.spokenText: What concerns me most is the lack of transparency.
options: What concerns me most is the lack of transparency.
What concern me most is the lack of transparency.
What concerns me most is the lacks of transparency.
What concerns me most is the lack of transparencies.
exercises.answer: What concerns me most is the lack of transparency.

exercises.prompt: 「It is the patient ___ deserves our attention.」(中文:「最值得我们关注的是病人。」)
「All I want is honesty」 用中文怎么说?
请组合出这个句子:「做出决定的是委员会,而不是某个个人。」
exercises.answer: It was the committee that made the decision not an individual

exercises.prompt: 「It was ___ here that we first met.」(中文:「我们当年正是在这里第一次相遇。」)

lessons.title: 分词从句
lessons.description: 用 -ing 和 -ed 构成的简短分句

exercises.prompt: 「她结束会议后离开了办公室」 用分词结构应该怎么写?
options: Finishing the meeting, she left the office.
Having finished the meeting, she left the office.
She finished meeting and left office.
exercises.answer: Having finished the meeting, she left the office.

exercises.prompt: 「___ in haste, the report contained errors.」(中文:「这份报告因写得仓促,含有错误。」)
请组合出这个句子:「她因为感到疲倦,早早就上床睡觉了。」
exercises.answer: Feeling tired she went to bed early

exercises.prompt: 「Approved by the board, the plan went ahead」 用中文怎么说?
options: Plan kurul tarafından onaylandığı için ilerledi.
exercises.answer: Plan kurul tarafından onaylandığı için ilerledi.

exercises.spokenText: Having reviewed the data, she drew her conclusions.
options: Having reviewed the data, she drew her conclusions.
Having review the data, she drew her conclusions.
Have reviewed the data, she drew her conclusions.
Having reviewed the data, she draw her conclusions.
exercises.answer: Having reviewed the data, she drew her conclusions.

exercises.prompt: 「___ at the airport, we headed to the hotel.」(中文:「到达机场之后,我们前往了酒店。」)
下列哪个分词结构是错误的?
options: Walking down the street, I saw an old friend.
Walked down the street, I saw an old friend.
Having walked down the street, I saw an old friend.
Being tired, I went to bed early.
exercises.answer: Walked down the street, I saw an old friend.

exercises.prompt: 请组合出这个句子:「这一被董事会审阅过的方案已获批准。」
exercises.answer: Reviewed by the board the plan was approved

exercises.prompt: 「___ ignored, the problem grew worse.」(中文:「问题在被忽视的过程中变得更加严重。」)
「It was the price that worried us」 是一个 ___ 句子。
exercises.explanation: 「It is/was X that…」 即为 it-分裂句结构。

exercises.prompt: 「___ I really want is a clear timeline.」(中文:「我真正想要的是一份清晰的时间表。」)(wh-cleft)
exercises.explanation: Wh-分裂句:「What I want is X.」

pairs.right: It was John who solved it.
What we need is more time.
Never have I seen such a thing.
It is essential that he attend.

exercises.prompt: 请组合出这个句子:「我们真正需要的是一份更清晰的简报。」
exercises.answer: What we really need is a clearer brief

exercises.prompt: 「Never have I encountered such resistance」 属于什么结构?
exercises.explanation: 当否定副词提前时,助动词需置于主语之前。

exercises.spokenText: Not until the audit was completed did we grasp the full picture.
options: Not until the audit was completed did we grasp the full picture.
Not until the audit was completed we grasped the full picture.
Not until the audit was completed did we grasped the full picture.
Not until the audits were completed do we grasp the full picture.
exercises.answer: Not until the audit was completed did we grasp the full picture.

exercises.prompt: 「It ___ not until 2020 that we noticed the trend.」(中文:「直到 2020 年我们才注意到这一趋势。」)(it-cleft)
下列哪一句是正确的前置(fronting)示例?
options: Rarely have we seen such growth.
Rarely we have seen such growth.
We rarely have seen such growth, however.
Have rarely we seen such growth.
exercises.answer: Rarely have we seen such growth.

exercises.prompt: 请组合出这个句子:「真正让我感到困扰的是透明度的缺乏。」
exercises.answer: What really troubled me was the lack of transparency

exercises.prompt: 「Only ___ examining the data did we identify the bias.」(中文:「直到检查完数据后,我们才识别出偏差。」)(前置 + 倒装)
exercises.explanation: 即 「Only after V-ing… did we…」 的结构。

exercises.prompt: 「It was Sarah who first raised the issue」 这一结构强调了什么?
请组合出这个句子:「在任何情况下我们都不会重回原协议。」
exercises.answer: Under no circumstances will we revert to the agreement

lessons.title: 高级关系从句与分词结构
lessons.description: 简化关系从句、分词从句、非限定结构

exercises.prompt: 「The report submitted yesterday is incomplete.」 属于什么结构?
exercises.explanation: 「which was submitted」 可简化为 「submitted」(过去分词短语)。

exercises.prompt: 「The candidate ___ for the role has fifteen years of experience.」(中文:「被选中担任这一职位的候选人具有十五年的经验。」)(分词)

pairs.right: 不可省略,省略后含义改变;不加逗号

exercises.prompt: 请组合出这个句子:「主导谈判的顾问今天将做汇报。」
exercises.answer: The consultant leading the negotiation will report today

exercises.prompt: 在 「The findings, which were unexpected, prompted further study」 中,为什么要加逗号?

exercises.spokenText: Having reviewed the proposal, we are prepared to move forward.
options: Having reviewed the proposal, we are prepared to move forward.
Having review the proposal, we are prepared to move forward.
Having reviewed the proposals, we is prepared to move forward.
Have reviewed the proposal, we are prepared to move forward.
exercises.answer: Having reviewed the proposal, we are prepared to move forward.

exercises.prompt: 「___ all things considered, the deal is fair.」(中文:「综合考虑一切因素,这笔交易是公平的。」)
exercises.explanation: 独立分词结构:「all things considered」。

exercises.prompt: 下列哪一句正确使用了分词从句?
options: Walking to work, my phone rang.
Walking to work, I noticed the new café.
Walking to work, the new café opened.
While walking to work, the new café was visible.
exercises.answer: Walking to work, I noticed the new café.
exercises.explanation: 分词的逻辑主语必须与主句一致:走路的是「I」,不是手机。

exercises.prompt: 请组合出这个句子:「考虑到所做的分析,这一结论是站得住脚的。」
exercises.answer: Given the analysis conducted the conclusion is defensible

exercises.prompt: 「The author, ___ work has shaped the field, will keynote.」(中文:「这位作品塑造了该领域的作者将担任主题演讲嘉宾。」)
「Rules permitting, we'll launch on Friday」 属于什么结构?
请组合出这个句子:「如果天气允许,开幕仪式将于明天举行。」
exercises.answer: Weather permitting the opening will take place tomorrow

lessons.title: 对话:与编辑就稿件展开拉锯
lessons.description: 通过分裂句与倒装句转移重音

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Your lede buries the actual story. The reader shouldn't have to wait three paragraphs to find out who did what to whom.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 为自己的写作辩护 — 用分裂句提出方案
options: Sure thing, I'll just put the answer in like the first sentence then.
What I was trying to foreground was the institutional context, not the individual actor — but I take your point and I'll restructure.
I don't get why you don't like it, it reads fine to me.
turns.answer: What I was trying to foreground was the institutional context, not the individual actor — but I take your point and I'll restructure.

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Foregrounding context is fine, but your verbs are limp. Half this draft is in passive voice.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 倒装强调 — 请补全助动词
turns.after: I revise the verbs, I'll also tighten the modifiers — the draft has accreted some lazy hedges.

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Good. And the kicker? It lands like a wet sponge. We need a closing line that actually closes.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 分裂句 + 建议 — 请选择自然的写作语言
options: It is precisely the absence of a verdict in the source material that I was trying to mirror — but I can sharpen the ambiguity into something more deliberate.
Yeah the ending sucks, my bad, I'll fix it.
Honestly endings are hard, can you just write it for me?
turns.answer: It is precisely the absence of a verdict in the source material that I was trying to mirror — but I can sharpen the ambiguity into something more deliberate.

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Sharpened ambiguity, I can work with. But the pull-quote needs an attribution; it's currently floating.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 分词结构 — 请填入正确的形式
turns.after: the source on background, I had to scrub the attribution — but I can negotiate a partial reveal with her press team.

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Negotiate hard. A floating quote in a piece this length will be picked apart on social.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 在书面话语中以 C1 水准收尾
options: Sure thing, I'll just text her or whatever.
Understood — I'll push for at least an on-the-record paraphrase and route the revision past you before filing.
turns.answer: Understood — I'll push for at least an on-the-record paraphrase and route the revision past you before filing.

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: By Thursday, please. We're holding the slot but I won't hold it indefinitely.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Thursday it is. I'll send the revised draft and a note flagging every change I've made.

topics.title: 辩论与演说
topics.description: 正式辩论中的话语语言

guide.intro: 正式辩论(debate)遵循特定结构:opening(开篇)、rebuttal(反驳)、summary(总结)。词汇选择反映出说话者的信念与逻辑。C1 阶段的说话者会将流利度与词汇的多样性结合起来。

rows: I'd like to begin by addressing…
With respect, I must take issue with…
The argument falls apart when we consider…
In conclusion, the case is clear: …

sections.text: 演说中的形容词选择决定语气。「Profound」 = 深刻;「compelling」 = 极具说服力;「tenuous」 = 脆弱、勉强;「specious」 = 看似合理实则站不住脚;「unfounded」 = 毫无根据。

rows.source: The argument is compelling, but ultimately flawed.
rows.translation: 论证颇具说服力,但最终仍存在缺陷。
这些指控完全没有依据。

rows.source: The reasoning, while seductive, is specious.
rows.translation: 论证看似诱人,实则似是而非。

sections.text: 在英语辩论中,「with respect」 实际上是用来软化反对的措辞。其作用相当于中文里的「恕我直言」或「请允许我冒昧地说」。

pairs.right: I'd like to begin by addressing…
With respect, I must take issue with…
The argument falls apart when we consider…

exercises.prompt: 「It is my contention that…」 用中文怎么说?
「With ___, I must disagree.」(中文:「恕我直言,我必须表示不同意。」)
请组合出这个句子:「在更深入审视后,这一论证便站不住脚了。」
exercises.answer: The argument falls apart on closer inspection

exercises.prompt: 下列哪个形容词用于描述「极具说服力的论证」?
「The reasoning is ___; it merely appears valid.」(中文:「这一论证看似成立,实则似是而非。」)
请组合出这个句子:「总而言之,该主张是站不住脚的。」
「I would ___ urge you to reconsider.」(中文:「我谨以敬意请您重新考虑。」)

lessons.title: 演说性形容词及其细微差别

exercises.prompt: 「The implications are ___」(中文:「其后果意味深远。」)
请组合出这个句子:「这个论证看似诱人,实则毫无根据。」
exercises.answer: The argument is seductive but unfounded

exercises.prompt: 哪个形容词承载着「看似有说服力但实则错误」的语气?

exercises.spokenText: The link between these variables is tenuous at best.
options: The link between these variables is tenuous at best.
The link between these variable is tenuous at best.
The link between these variables is tenuous at beast.
The link between these variables are tenuous at best.
exercises.answer: The link between these variables is tenuous at best.

exercises.prompt: 「These accusations are ___」(中文:「这些指控毫无根据。」)
请组合出这个句子:「这不是严谨的分析,只是空泛的揣测。」
exercises.answer: This is not rigorous analysis but mere speculation

exercises.prompt: 「Their reasoning is ___ flawed.」(中文:「他们的论证从根本上就是错误的。」)
话语标记词 — 中文释义
「___ his concerns, the project went ahead.」(中文:「尽管他有所担忧,项目仍然向前推进。」)
请组合出这个句子:「诚然,这个想法很诱人,然而它并不可行。」
exercises.answer: Granted the idea is appealing however it is not feasible

exercises.prompt: 「The market has shifted; ___, our strategy must adapt.」(中文:「市场已经发生变化,因此我们的战略必须随之调整。」)
下列哪个话语标记起到「让步」的作用?
请组合出这个句子:「相反,在小规模分析中呈现出不同的趋势。」
exercises.answer: Conversely the smaller scale analysis shows a different trend

exercises.prompt: 「___ the criticism, the policy stands.」(中文:「尽管面临批评,该政策依然有效。」)

lessons.title: 反驳模式(rebuttal)
lessons.description: 公平地复述对方论点,然后将其击倒

exercises.prompt: 下列哪一句是公平的「反驳」(rebuttal)的开头?
options: If I understand the argument correctly, …
exercises.answer: If I understand the argument correctly, …

exercises.prompt: 「The argument ___ on a questionable assumption.」(中文:「这一论证依赖于一个值得商榷的假设。」)

pairs.right: 指出对方混淆了两个不同概念

pairs.left: The evidence cuts the other way

exercises.prompt: 请组合出这个句子:「该论证将结构性原因与个人选择混为一谈。」

topics.title: 艺术与评论

guide.intro: 艺术评论英语是一种需要精细把握的语域。人们用 「accomplished」、「derivative」、「evocative」、「heavy-handed」 这类形容词来取代 「good」、「bad」。中文里的「经典」「悲剧」「讽刺」与英文同源词看似对应,但语义范围更窄:「a classic film」 = 某类型的代表作;「tragedy」 是文学体裁;「ironic」 是与预期相反(中文里常被错用为「巧合」)。

sections.text: 在 C1 阶段的评论写作中,直接说「好」或「坏」显得乏力。「Accomplished」(精湛)和 「masterful」(炉火纯青)用于褒奖;「derivative」(模仿性强)、「contrived」(刻意)、「pretentious」(故作姿态)、「heavy-handed」(粗笨)则用于批评。

rows.source: The film struck a chord with audiences worldwide.
rows.translation: 这部电影触动了全球观众的心弦。

rows.source: The novel falls flat in its final act.
rows.translation: 小说在最后一幕里失去了张力。

rows.source: It is a tour de force of contemporary cinema.
rows.translation: 是当代电影中的一部杰作。

rows.source: A slow burn that rewards patient viewers.
rows.translation: 是一部慢热但回报耐心观众的作品。

rows.source: The album was ahead of its time.
rows.translation: 这张专辑超越了它所处的时代。

rows.source: It's a guilty pleasure of mine.
rows.translation: 是我难以承认却确实喜欢的「秘密快乐」。

sections.text: 中文里的「艺术」涵盖手工艺;但英文 「art」 范围更窄,通常与高雅文化挂钩。表示手工艺时请用 「crafts」 或 「craftsmanship」。
中文里「经典的」有时也带有「典型的/老套的」之意(例如「典型错误」)。但英文 「a classic」 仅指「某类别中的杰出范例」;「典型错误」 = 「a textbook mistake」。

topics.title: 新闻与评论专栏
topics.description: 新闻、分析与评论专栏语域中的高级英语

guide.intro: 新闻英语包含三种不同的语域:纯报道(reporting)、分析(analysis)与评论专栏(editorial / op-ed)。中文里的「新闻语言」看起来像是一种统一的范式,但在英语中,即便最微小的语气变化 —— 用 「claimed」 替换 「said」、用 「alleged」 替换 「reported」 —— 都会改变含义。

sections.text: Reporting 追求客观中立(「Officials announced…」)。Analysis 对数据进行解读(「What this means for…」)。Editorial / op-ed 则会表明立场(「It is high time we…」)。混用这三种语域是严重的语域错误。

rows: According to officials, the bill passed…
What this means for the wider economy…
It is high time we addressed…

rows.source: according to sources familiar with the matter
rows.translation: 据熟悉此事的消息人士透露

rows.source: amid concerns that markets may overheat
rows.translation: 在市场可能过热的担忧之中

rows.source: officials say no decision has been made
rows.translation: 官员表示尚未做出决定

rows.source: the spokesperson did not immediately respond

items: alleged:据称(尚未被证实)
claimed:声称(引述中带有距离感)
reportedly:据报道(确定性较低)
purportedly:声称的、所谓的(带怀疑色彩)
ostensibly:表面上(真实意图可能并非如此)

sections.text: 新闻标题中冠词通常被省略(「Senate Passes Budget」),用现在时表示过去事件(「Court Rules Against…」),使用冒号加引号的格式(「Minister: "This is a turning point"」),并以来源后缀结尾(「…: Report」)。
评论文章中常见的套路化表达:「It is high time we…」、「One could argue…」、「Make no mistake…」、「Far from being a panacea…」。这些句式是 op-ed 与评论文章的标志;若用于纯报道,则属于严重的语域错位。

lessons.title: Reporting / Analysis / Editorial 之间的区分

exercises.prompt: 「It is high time we acted on this.」 的语气如何?

Op-ed 套路化表达 — 中文释义

exercises.answer: Make no mistake this is the end of an era

exercises.prompt: 在 op-ed 中最合适的开头是哪一句?
options: It is high time we confronted the issue.
The court issued its ruling at noon.
exercises.answer: It is high time we confronted the issue.

exercises.spokenText: Far from being a panacea, the proposal raises more questions than it answers.
options: Far from being a panacea, the proposal raises more questions than it answers.
Far from a panacea, the proposal raises more questions than it answers.
Far from being a panacea, the proposals raises more questions than it answer.
Far from being a panaceas, the proposal raises more questions than it answers.
exercises.answer: Far from being a panacea, the proposal raises more questions than it answers.

exercises.prompt: 「I, for ___, find the argument unconvincing.」(中文:「至少在我看来,这一论证并不具有说服力。」)

exercises.prompt: 请组合出这个句子:「这并不只是一个简单的监管问题。」

lessons.description: 从片段中推断语域与立场

exercises.prompt: 「It is high time the regulator stepped in.」 属于哪种语域?

We urge lawmaker, in the strongest possible terms, to reconsider.
We urges lawmakers, in the strongest possible terms, to reconsider.
We urge lawmakers, in the strongest possible term, to reconsider.
exercises.answer: We urge lawmakers, in the strongest possible terms, to reconsider.

lessons.title: 对话:在电台访谈中回应记者的提问
lessons.description: 关于某条新闻的访谈 — 受访者视角

exercises.prompt: 电台节目 — 关于一项法案的质询

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: You've been one of the most vocal critics of the bill. Give our listeners the headline — what's at stake here?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 访谈开场 — 用分裂句转移重音
options: Basically the bill is dumb and everyone should hate it.
What's at stake isn't the headline number but the precedent — once this mechanism is in statute, future governments will reach for it reflexively.
Idk the bill exists and we're against it I guess.
turns.answer: What's at stake isn't the headline number but the precedent — once this mechanism is in statute, future governments will reach for it reflexively.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Supporters argue the safeguards are robust. Are they wrong, in your view?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 正式让步状语 — 请填空
turns.after: the safeguards look robust on paper, the enforcement mechanism is funded for two years and reviewed by the very ministry it constrains.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That sounds like a charge of bad faith. Are you saying the drafters knew?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 作为受访者使用模糊语 — 避免下结论
options: I'd stop short of imputing motive — but I'd note that the structural weakness is too convenient to be accidental, and that's a question for the legislators to answer.
I have no idea, don't ask me.
turns.answer: I'd stop short of imputing motive — but I'd note that the structural weakness is too convenient to be accidental, and that's a question for the legislators to answer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Let me push back. Polling shows the public broadly supports the bill. Doesn't that count for something?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 倒装强调 — 请补全助动词
turns.after: I dismiss the polling — but support softens markedly once respondents see the enforcement clause, which is rarely included in the surveys.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: If you could rewrite one clause tonight, which would it be?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 请选择一个具体、便于媒体引用的回答
options: Just delete the whole thing tbh.
I'd hand the review function to an independent body with multi-year funding and the power to compel disclosure — without that, the rest is window-dressing.
Idk man, hard to say in a sound bite.
turns.answer: I'd hand the review function to an independent body with multi-year funding and the power to compel disclosure — without that, the rest is window-dressing.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: We're nearly out of time. Final thought for the audience?

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Read the enforcement clause, not the press release. The press release will not be what governs your life.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Thank you for joining us. That was a sharper conversation than most of us were expecting tonight.

topics.title: C1 — 总复习
topics.description: 综合 C1 所有主题的复习

guide.intro: 本部分将 C1 阶段涵盖的商务、学术、社会、习语、语法和辩论等主题融为一体。每道练习都会触及多个主题。

items: 我能在商务文件中保持一致的正式语域。
我能在学术写作中恰当地使用模糊语。
我能在社会议题讨论中选用具有细微差别的形容词。
我能识别常见习语以及容易混淆的「假朋友」。
我能熟练使用倒装与分裂句。
我能用话语标记词(granted、conversely、hence)衔接句子。

exercises.prompt: 「Pursuant to our discussion」 用中文怎么翻译?
「A growing ___ of evidence indicates climate sensitivity.」(中文:「越来越多的证据表明气候敏感性。」)

exercises.spokenText: Critics argue the policy is short-sighted.

Critic argue the policy is short-sighted.
Critics argues the policy is short-sighted.
Critics argue the policies is short-sighted.

exercises.prompt: 中文里的「检查/核对」对应英语中的哪个词?
exercises.explanation: 假朋友!英文 「control」 主要意味着「掌控、支配」,而不是「检查/核对」。

What concerns me most is lacks of transparency.

lessons.title: 对话:高级顾问客户会议
lessons.description: 综合场景 — 观点、语域与习语

exercises.prompt: 客户会议 — 关于整体重组的建议

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: We've read the deck. Cut to the chase — do you genuinely think a wholesale restructure is warranted, or is this consultant theatre?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 开场 — 用分裂句给出诚实的判断
options: Yeah it's basically theatre but you're paying us so we did it.
What the analysis points to isn't theatre — the cost-to-serve gap is structural, and incremental fixes will compound rather than close it.
Honestly the deck is whatever, look at the cover slide.
turns.answer: What the analysis points to isn't theatre — the cost-to-serve gap is structural, and incremental fixes will compound rather than close it.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: To build on that — the diagnostic is consistent across three independent data cuts, which gives us a level of conviction we don't always have at this stage.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Conviction is one thing. The board will want to know what the downside looks like if we move and the macro turns.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 正式条件状语 — 请填空
turns.after: the macro deteriorate further, the restructure actually shortens your cash runway by six to eight months, so the move is risk-reducing, not risk-adding.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: And the people piece? We've burned the workforce twice in five years. Another round and morale won't recover.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 习语 + 语域 — 请选出合适的回答
options: Honestly people get over it, that's life.
It's a fair concern — and one we'd want to handle with extreme care; the literature on change fatigue is unambiguous, and we'd recommend front-loading transparency rather than drip-feeding bad news.
Just rip the band-aid off bro, they'll deal.
turns.answer: It's a fair concern — and one we'd want to handle with extreme care; the literature on change fatigue is unambiguous, and we'd recommend front-loading transparency rather than drip-feeding bad news.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: We've sequenced the communications plan so the operating model is settled before the headcount conversation — that's a hard-won lesson from comparable programmes.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 倒装强调 — 请补全助动词
turns.before: Only by settling the operating model first
turns.after: we credibly tell people what their roles will look like — and that, in our experience, is the single biggest determinant of retention.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Suppose I greenlight Phase 1 tomorrow. What's the first thing that's going to go wrong, and how do we get ahead of it?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 请选出一个习语化的 C1 收尾
options: Nothing will go wrong, trust me bro.
Idk we'll just figure it out when it happens lol.
Mid-level managers will read the org chart before the narrative lands — so we'd want a cascade briefing inside forty-eight hours, otherwise the grapevine writes the story for you.
turns.answer: Mid-level managers will read the org chart before the narrative lands — so we'd want a cascade briefing inside forty-eight hours, otherwise the grapevine writes the story for you.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Useful. Send me a revised mobilisation plan by Wednesday and I'll take it to the board.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Will do. We'll route a draft past your CFO first so the numbers are unimpeachable before the board sees them.
